newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav airline increases international flights.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav airline increases international flights.

text.p: Yugoslav airlines Jugoslovenski Aerotransport (JAT) said on Friday it will introduce a flight to St. Petersburg in its summer timetable.
JAT will start flying to St. Petersburg from May 30, raising the total number of international destinations from the present 29 to 30, JAT said in a press release.
The number of flights to most European destinations will be increased in the summer timetable, effective from March 30 to October 25.
There will be daily flights to Amsterdam and Zurich, and one additional flight per week to Frankfurt, Prague and Vienna.
At the height of the summer season, JAT will have extra flights to Duesseldorf, Berlin, Stuttgart, and Skopje as well.
In the interval between June 2 and August 25, JAT will fly separately to Stockholm and Goeteborg in Sweden, previously a single route.
From May 19, JAT will again start flying to Barcelona, Spain.
The number of international flights to Montenegro will be raised with one direct weekly flight each from Duesseldorf and Tel Aviv to Tivat, and one from St. Petersburg to Podgorica.

From mid-June to mid-September there will be seven daily flights from Belgrade to Tivat on the Montenegrin coast and three to Podgorica. JAT also plans to link Nis, Pristina and Uzice to Tivat at the peak of the tourist season.

Besides the regular schedule, JAT plans to open seasonal runs to Ohrid, Corfu, Rhodes, Palma de Mallorca, Ismir, Tunis and other cities, depending on interest. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
